businessProfile.productSummary: A women's sustainable activewear line made from recycled ocean plastic, sold as premium performance / lifestyle pieces.
businessProfile.brandVoice: values-driven, confident, female-forward (premium + sustainability; authentic, non-corporate)

assumptions: Primary market is the U.S. (catalog is U.S.-focused and advertiser gave no geo).
Product AOV estimated ~USD 120 based on being priced between Lululemon and Girlfriend Collective.
Target age-skew is adults 25-44 who buy premium activewear.
Distribution is DTC / apparel retail (ecommerce) rather than grocery or subscriptions.
clarifyingQuestions: What is the typical price range (SKU price or cart AOV) you expect per order?
Which geographies or U.S. regions are priority (nationwide or specific coasts/metros)?
What are your top-selling SKUs (leggings, bras, sets) and primary channels (DTC site, marketplaces, wholesale)?
Do you have sustainability certifications or measurable claims (e.g., % recycled content, third-party certs) we should highlight?

reasons: Subcategories explicitly include activewear and sustainable, matching product category and sustainability positioning.
AOV USD 118 is tightly aligned with the brand's premium price point (~USD 120 estimate).
Audience age skew (25-45) and notes call out comfort + sustainability messaging — exactly the brand claims that convert here.
Category is apparel with an activewear subcategory and a heavily female audience (82% female; age skew 25-44), matching target shoppers.
Notes describe 'fitness-engaged shoppers' with crossover to wellness — high purchase intent for performance sustainable activewear.
Monthly impressions (22M) provide scale for performance and brand campaigns to reach an engaged audience.
Publisher focuses on women and sustainable shoes (apparel-adjacent) with explicit sustainable positioning and high-income, female-skewed audience (94% female).
AOV USD 142 indicates an audience accustomed to premium price points, useful for a brand positioned above mainstream but below luxury.
Notes call out that sustainability claims resonate, which aligns with recycled ocean-plastic messaging.
Strong reach among Gen Z / younger millennial women (91% female; age skew 18-34) who discover brands via identity and aesthetic, aiding early-funnel discovery.
Notes indicate a minimalist, identity-driven audience—useful for building brand affinity and social creative that highlights values and look.
While category is beauty rather than apparel, the audience's discovery behavior and high values-alignment make this a viable upper-funnel partner.
Apparel publisher focused on basics with social-good responsiveness in notes, meaning the audience cares about mission-driven brands.
Female-leaning audience and experience with gifting season (Nov-Dec) can help capture gift purchases and basics cross-sell.
Although AOV (USD 52) is lower than the brand estimate, the publisher's social-good signal and apparel context support customer acquisition and entry-level buys.

excludedPublishers.reason: Instant-delivery convenience/grocery channel with AOV USD 28 and impulse mindset is not a likely place for premium sustainable activewear purchases.
Studiogrid is appointment-based wellness services (fitness classes/spa) where users spend on services, not apparel shopping; limited direct apparel purchase intent.
Marlowe & Co. targets older mid-life workwear shoppers (age 45-65) who prioritize classic workwear over premium activewear.
Linden Park skews 50-70 and focuses on classic/workwear with very high AOV—audience unlikely to shop for trend-forward sustainable activewear.
Everbody specializes in inclusive plus-size workwear/intimates with an older age skew (30-55) and fit/representation focus rather than sustainable active performance apparel.
Pawline is a pet channel (pet food/supplies) where purchase intent is pet-related despite some audience overlap in demographics.
Pantrygood is organic grocery-focused; while shoppers care about sustainability, they do not primarily shop for apparel on this publisher.
Ruffco is a pet retailer with broad reach but its commerce intent centers on pet products, not women's activewear.
Northbed focuses on high-AOV home textiles and design-conscious home shoppers, not apparel purchase intent for activewear.
Daily Form is wellness DTC focused on supplements and subscription products—audience is female-wellness oriented but this publisher's commerce is health products, not apparel.
Hearthstone Goods targets high-AOV kitchen/sustainability-motivated kitchen buyers whose purchase behavior is appliance/kitchen-focused, not apparel.
Kitchenly is meal-kit focused (families/couples) where conversion behavior is food/subscription-oriented rather than apparel shopping.
Tailcrate is pet-supply/subscription with playful brand voice; purchase intent is dog-related, not women's activewear.
Strandlab centers on personalized haircare DTC and quiz-based onboarding—useful for discovery but not a natural commerce surface for premium activewear.
Pop & Sip is functional beverages with an audience that overlaps wellness, but the publisher's commerce and category focus are beverage-first, not apparel.

selectedPersonas.whyRelevant: This persona purchases specifically based on environmental footprint, researches supply chains, and is willing to pay more for genuinely sustainable apparel—direct match for recycled-ocean-plastic activewear.
selectedPersonas.keyMessage: Verified sustainability: high recycled-content activewear with transparent supply chain and certifications — premium performance without greenwashing.

selectedPersonas.whyRelevant: Fitness Enthusiast buys performance activewear and values technical fabric and endorsements; they will pay for gear that performs and lasts.
selectedPersonas.keyMessage: Performance-first sustainable pieces — technical fabrics and athlete-vetted fit made from recycled ocean plastic.

selectedPersonas.whyRelevant: Gen Z Aesthete discovers via aesthetic and values-driven storytelling; they amplify brands that look and stand for something, aiding social discovery and word-of-mouth.
selectedPersonas.keyMessage: Look good, do good: stylish, Instagram-ready activewear made from ocean plastics that signals your values.

selectedPersonas.whyRelevant: Wellness Optimizer is premium, evidence-focused, and pays for outcome-based products; they intersect with premium activewear and value transparent, credible claims.
selectedPersonas.keyMessage: Sustainable performance backed by material science: measurable recycled content and durability for daily training and recovery.

variants.headline: Premium activewear made from recycled ocean plastic—no greenwash
variants.body: High recycled-content performance pieces for women, made from recycled ocean plastic. We publish material and supply-chain breakdowns so you can verify sourcing and impact—premium fit positioned between Lululemon and Girlfriend Collective.
variants.rationale: Directly addresses a sustainability buyer’s demand for specific recycled-content, supply-chain transparency, and a premium positioning while rejecting vague eco-speak.

variants.headline: Train harder: performance-first activewear made from ocean plastic
variants.body: Premium women’s pieces built for regular training—performance-focused construction and a supportive fit, made from recycled ocean plastic. Durable, movement-ready gear for 4+ workouts a week without sacrificing sustainability.
variants.rationale: Speaks the fitness enthusiast’s language—performance-first, durable, and built for frequent training—while keeping the sustainable material front and center.

variants.headline: Look good, do good: Instagram-ready activewear from ocean plastics
variants.body: Vibe-forward styles and clean silhouettes made from recycled ocean plastic. Wearable on and off the mat, these premium pieces let you signal your values with a confident, female-forward look that plays well on Reels and IRL.
variants.rationale: Uses aesthetic-forward, playful language and values alignment to appeal to a Gen Z buyer who prioritizes look, voice, and signaling over corporate-sounding claims.

variants.headline: Sustainable performance backed by material transparency
variants.body: High recycled-content activewear engineered for daily training and recovery. Made from recycled ocean plastic with a focus on durability and documented material specs—premium performance between Lululemon and Girlfriend Collective.
variants.rationale: Emphasizes measurable recycled content, durability, and material documentation to match a wellness optimizer’s preference for science-backed, outcome-focused details.

bidStrategy.rationale: Considered purchase at ~$120 AOV: bid to a target CPA of 20-35% of order value so first-order economics stay profitable

budget.rationale: $1500/publisher/month floor for statistically useful volume × 5 publishers × 1.25 premium-tier multiplier
